Original SASRec scales sequence input embeddings by √d, retains unscaled candidate embeddings, and applies final LayerNorm before dot-product scoring ([source code](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), [embedding implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py)). Consequently, scaling recent_pool changes its strength relative to h; scaling candidate embeddings changes logit magnitude. A common positive score multiplier preserves fixed-model rankings but changes training losses and gradients. Extra LayerNorm can change rankings through centering and learned coordinate-wise affine parameters; it is not merely temperature scaling.

By differentiation, for z=LN(h+σ(a)p), ∂L/∂a=σ(a)(1−σ(a))·(∇zL)ᵀJ_LN p. At a=−4, the gate is approximately 0.018 and its derivative 0.0177: small, but effective mixing also depends on ‖p‖/‖h‖ and direction. LayerNorm suppresses perturbations along the all-ones direction and approximately along the centered input. Neither a finite sigmoid gate nor a fresh LN initialized with γ=1, β=0 guarantees baseline equivalence. Exact initialization can use z=h+αp with α=0, or replace the existing final LN with LN_existing(u+αp), α=0, where h=LN_existing(u). Zero-initialized residual gates follow [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887).

Use matched ablations: unchanged baseline h; normalization-only LN_extra(h); pooling-only h+gp; combined LN_extra(h+gp). Preserve embedding scaling, candidate scoring, initialization, training settings and evaluation across comparisons. Separately compare raw versus √d-scaled pools, fixed versus learned gates, and baseline plus a scalar score temperature. Check initial score equality for baseline-equivalent variants; log pool/feature norms, gate values, gate gradients and logit spread. These controls distinguish pooling benefits from normalization and training-scale effects; no gain follows from the equations alone.
